classification.difficultyReason: Generalise coordinate differences to derive the internal division formula for an arbitrary ratio.

content.prompt: The point $P$ divides the interval $AB$ in the ratio $m:n$. That is $AP:PB=m:n$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

spec.description: Coordinate axes and an ascending segment with points in the order A, P, B. Diagram coordinates control presentation only and supply no numerical givens. Decorative source blue and red are replaced by ordinary black marks; the origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: A has coordinates (x_1,y_1), B has coordinates (x_2,y_2), and the internal point P has coordinates (x,y). AP:PB=m:n; no midpoint or equal-length marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All endpoint and point-coordinate labels are permanent givens; the section formula is answer-only.

answer.short:
$P\left(\dfrac{nx_1+mx_2}{m+n},\dfrac{ny_1+my_2}{m+n}\right)$.

Move the fraction $\dfrac{m}{m+n}$ of each coordinate difference from $A$ towards $B$.
answer.worked:
Since $AP:PB=m:n$, $AP$ is $\dfrac{m}{m+n}$ of $AB$. Apply this fraction to each coordinate difference.
$$\begin{align*}x&=x_1+\frac{m}{m+n}(x_2-x_1)\\x&=\frac{(m+n)x_1+mx_2-mx_1}{m+n}\\x&=\frac{nx_1+mx_2}{m+n}\\y&=y_1+\frac{m}{m+n}(y_2-y_1)\\y&=\frac{(m+n)y_1+my_2-my_1}{m+n}\\y&=\frac{ny_1+my_2}{m+n}\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $P\left(\dfrac{nx_1+mx_2}{m+n},\dfrac{ny_1+my_2}{m+n}\right)$.
